column4: thm:mf-quotient-units proof, sentence 1: "The ring M_n(R) is again countable, purely infinite, and simple [AGP, Corollary 1.7], and K_1(M_n(R)) = K_1(R) by Morita invariance, so it suffices to treat n=1." UPDATED 2026-09-09 (lane o-morita, new modules KOne/MoritaKOne.lean and Manuscript/OneSidedMFRadical/MFQuotientUnitsKOneMorita.lean). The earlier note on this row says the Morita clause "has no separate carrier and needs none". The second half stays true: the conclusion is reached without Morita (MFQuotientCanonicalKOne.manuscriptMFQuotientUnitsKOneAtBaseRing compares GL_n(R) with K_1(R) through the rank-n map matrixKappa). The first half is now false: the printed clause is PROVED. morita_algebraicKOne gives K_1(M_n(R)) = K_1(R) for an ARBITRARY unital ring and every n >= 1, with no countability, simplicity or purely infinite hypothesis, by flattening GL_m(M_n R) = GL_{mn}(R) and the cofinality of m -> mn; moritaKOne discharges the hypothesis Prop MFQuotientUnitsKOne.MoritaKOne, which is therefore no longer an obligation anywhere; moritaKOneEquiv_matrixKappa shows the Morita identification composed with the printed kappa of M_n(R) is exactly matrixKappa R n, so the two routes to the printed conclusion agree on the comparison maps and not only on the groups.
